questions.q: What is one major item that India provides to Nepal as part of their trade relationship?
questions.a: India supplies fuel and manufactured goods to Nepal. A wrong answer here suggests the student has not grasped the concept that trade involves sending finished products or energy to neighbors who need them.

questions.q: Why does sharing an open border with a country like Nepal make trade "substantial"?
questions.a: An open border allows goods to move freely by road without complex obstacles, making trade faster and cheaper. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks trade only happens by sea or air, missing the importance of land connectivity.

questions.q: If Bhutan has a lot of mountain rivers, what is one useful product India might import from them?
questions.a: India imports hydroelectric power. The student must apply the logic that a country's natural geography (mountains/rivers) dictates what they can sell to others.

questions.q: How does the trade relationship between India and its neighbors benefit the common people in both countries?
questions.a: It ensures that neighbors get essential items like food or fuel quickly, while Indian farmers and businesses get a market to sell their products. A wrong answer shows a lack of understanding that trade is a two-way street for mutual survival.

questions.q: Is trade only about selling things, or is there another part to it? Justify your answer.
questions.a: Trade is both selling (exporting) and buying (importing) to balance needs. A wrong answer fails to recognize that countries are interdependent and cannot produce everything they need on their own.

questions.q: Imagine India and a neighbor suddenly stopped all trade. What would happen to the price of goods in both countries? Explain your reasoning.
questions.a: Prices would rise because goods would become scarce or have to be brought from much further away, increasing transport costs. A poor answer ignores the economic principle of supply and demand.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Trade and economic relations refer to the exchange of goods, resources, and services between India and its ______ countries to support mutual economic development.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever ______ your extra pens for a friend's eraser during class?
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to list at least three specific trade items exchanged between India and its neighbors and explain why proximity (like borders) influences the ease of this trade.
